title: Forest & Bird says personal data from website forms was accessed in a cyber incident
date_note: Published November 20; the article does not say when the access happened or was found.
geo_basis: organisation country; Wellington used as the national point
summary: New Zealand conservation charity Forest & Bird told people that personal information they gave through a website form was accessed without authorisation. The data may include names, phone numbers and email addresses. Chief executive Sam Rowland said the access was blocked and malicious files removed, and that the Privacy Commissioner, police and the National Cyber Security Centre were told. No number of people was given.
plain: A New Zealand conservation charity says hackers got names, phone numbers and email addresses that people entered on its website forms. Scam messages could follow.
exec: A well-known charity's supporter data was exposed; it shows how web form data can fuel convincing donation scams.
action: If you gave Forest & Bird details online, treat unexpected messages with caution; donations only via payments.forestandbird.org.nz and email only from @forestandbird.org.nz.
impact: Names, phone numbers and email addresses of people who used Forest & Bird website forms may be affected; the number is not stated.

validation.note: NZ Herald (Neil Reid, 20 Nov) quoting Forest & Bird's email to affected people and statement from chief executive Sam Rowland.

review.note: Compared title, date (20 Nov), data types (name, phone, email, may include), no count, Rowland blocked/removed-files quote, Privacy Commissioner/police/NCSC notification, no actor and scam advice against the NZ Herald article; status confirmed by the charity's own email
